n: Vision four: a heavenly courtroom. Joshua the high priest stands before the angel of the Lord, and Satan (“the accuser”) stands ready to accuse him.
The Lord rebukes the accuser. Isn’t Joshua a burning stick snatched from the fire — rescued from exile? God defends those He has saved.

f.w: a brand plucked out of the fire

n: Joshua stands dressed in filthy clothes — representing his sin and the sin of the people he represents.

f.g: Hebrew suggests clothing soiled with excrement — the vilest uncleanness.

n: The angel orders the filthy clothes removed: “I have taken away your sin and will clothe you in fine garments.” A powerful image of forgiveness through the Savior’s Atonement.

f.w: I have caused thine iniquity to pass from thee

n: Zechariah himself speaks up: “Put a clean turban on his head!” Joshua is fully restored to priestly service.

f.g: The high priest’s turban, which bore the words “Holiness to the Lord” (Exodus 28:36-38).

n: The angel of the Lord then solemnly charges Joshua.
If Joshua walks in God’s ways and keeps His charge, he will govern God’s house and courts and have access among those standing in God’s presence. Forgiveness invites faithful service.

f.w: places to walk among these that stand by
f.g: Access to God’s presence, among the angels who serve Him.

n: Joshua and his fellow priests are a sign of something to come: God will bring His servant, the Branch — a title of the Messiah from David’s line.

f.g: Men who are a sign or omen.

n: A stone with seven eyes is set before Joshua. God will engrave it and remove the land’s sin in a single day — many Christians see this fulfilled in Christ’s atoning sacrifice.
In that day everyone will invite neighbors to sit under their vine and fig tree — a picture of peace and security.

f.w: under the vine and under the fig tree
